item.content:encoded:
Plagiarism is pretty easy to track on the site, since every time you make an edit on a page, the revision is noted, along with the time/date/comparison option. If staff finds that someone's material matches yours and you have the earliest edit history, things look heavily in your favor.

That said, I highly doubt anyone would bother camping sandboxes to swipe contest material. Your sandbox is only viewed if you ask for it—again, either on chat or forums. If you don't ask for it, people won't review it.

If you're really uncomfortable about people seeing your work, you can always private message a staff member. I'm pretty sure there are a decent number of them who won't be participating in the contest (myself included), so if you want to double-check your piece but don't want it in the public eye, there's that option. There's less of a chance you'll get an in-depth review, though.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
It's a matter of head canon. Each of us has a different concept of what the Foundation actually is, and certainly they are not "the nicest group out there", not by a long shot. In a way, even the Coalition, who wish to save the world by ending anomalies, are "good guys"; extremists and mass-murderers to the Serpent's Hand, yes, but trying to save a clueless humanity. In a way, even the Serpent's Hand is trying to do the right thing, by giving the destitute anomalies, sentient and sapient, a future in a world scared of them, unfit for them.

Then we have the Horizon Initiative, that tries to be fair in its decisions, as guided from its own moral compass. Then we have doctor Wondertainment, who, let's be fair, is clearly not evil. And the Manna Charitable Foundation is certainly not the bad guys.

In fact, pretty much every group is in a clear, solidly defined global ground of "yes, this is nice, this is not." The Foundation is defined as a completely amoral organisation, which is, yes, why this world could be considered a dystopia… if you wanna believe they have all that much power.

In my head canon, the Foundation is not that large, nor that powerful, nor that discreet. They do what they do to understand anomalies, contain them and protect humanity, being decidedly inhuman in the process; evil? Not really, no. Just immensely ambiguous.
